summary: `@Plot` is a tag from the `garden-kit` toolbox. It does nothing while the planner runs. It only matters to the seed printer: it reads the tag and writes the `name` and `notes` onto the packet labels that gardeners see.
keep-out: **Decision: keep them out.** The 40 herbs with no entry in the seed catalogue (wild mint, sea kale, and 12 others) stay out of this season's plan. A later season adds them bed by bed, with someone who knows the soil.
verbatim: **Decision: copy the catalogue as is.** The catalogue's growing notes go in exactly as printed, odd spellings and missing full stops included. The 30 corrections from the first read (spellings, units, one plant name) move to the follow-up plan, where they are a tidy change of their own.
columns:
| On the packet | In the planner | Who uses it |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `name:` | gardeners, as the bed's heading |
| `notes` | `notes:` | gardeners |
| `sun = full` | the bed's `sun:` field | gardeners and tools: "needs full sun" |
| `spacing` | `spacing:` | gardeners and tools, e.g. `30cm` |
| `season` | `season:` | gardeners and tools: a closed list |
| `@Tip(text = "…")` | `x-tip: "…"` | gardeners only; tools ignore `x-` keys |
sheet:
The seed catalogue describes each plant in four columns. Three of them have a home in the planner. The fourth, **Tips**, does not:
PlantDescriptionBedTips
TomatoStatus of the seedling traySunnyWater at: dawn dusk
Never at: noon
BasilLeafy, likes warmthPotPinch the flowers off
The tips column is free text, so a reader cannot rely on its shape.
applied:
**Decided: standard fields, and the tip in the notes.** No custom field.

Planted as **trial** beds in 6 plots, and `garden-plan.yaml` redrawn. The watering schedule passes.

- `x-tip` and the `@Tip` tags are gone: 0 left.
- Every catalogue tip now follows the plant's notes after a blank line and a `**Tip:**` label, verbatim.
- `sun` and `spacing` stay as they were.
- `season` was added to the 5 vegetables whose tip lists the months.
- `harvest` was **not** added. The catalogue says only "summer", which doesn't say early or late, so picking one would be guessing.

```java
@Plot(name = "Tomato",
    notes = "Status of the seedling tray\n\n"
        + "**Tip:** Water at: `dawn` `dusk`",
    season = {"may", "june", "july"})
String status,
```
yaml:
```yaml
status:
  type: string
  name: Tomato
  notes: Status of the seedling tray
  season: [may, june, july]
```

The redrawn plan, after the change.
survey:
## What other planners do

I tried three made-up planners and how they carry this kind of tip: [one](https://example.com/planners/one), [two](https://example.com/planners/two) and [three](https://example.test/three).

* Two put it in the `notes`.
* One uses an `x-` field that no tool reads.

### Verdict

The notes are the place *readers* look first.
